title: Drug formulations, biologicals drive pharma exports up 5.7%

contentHtml:
Synopsis

Pharmaceutical exports from India reached approximately $18.89 billion during the first seven months of fiscal year 2027. Imports experienced a slower growth, rising to $5.65 billion in the same period. The United States maintained its status as the largest export destination, despite a slight decline year-on-year. Brazil showed strong growth as the second-largest destination for India's pharmaceutical products.

New Delhi: India's pharmaceutical exports grew 5.68% to about $18.89 billion during the April-October period of fiscal 2027, while imports increased at a slower pace of just over 3% to $5.65 billion, according to data compiled by the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics.

In October, pharmaceutical exports increased 10.55% from a year earlier to $2.7 billion. Compared with September, shipments rose 0.27%.

Exports of drug formulations and biologicals grew 4.71% and remained the largest category at 73.86% of the total shipments, the data showed.

Bulk drugs and drug intermediates posted a 14.62% increase in shipments in the seven-month period to $3.2 billion, accounting for 17.07% of total exports.

Exports of surgical products increased 10.62% to $506.9 million, while Ayush and herbal products grew 2.64% to $385.8 million. Vaccine exports declined 9.09% to $819.5 million.

The US continued to be India's largest pharmaceutical export destination, accounting for 29.48% of total exports. However, shipments to the country declined 2.01% year-on-year to about $5.6 billion during April-October FY27.

Brazil emerged as the second-largest destination, with exports rising 18% to $605.2 million. Exports to the UK increased 3.21% to $537.5 million, while shipments to France and the Netherlands grew 13.78% and 16.74%, respectively.

Germany recorded a 24.05% increase in imports from India to $427.3 million. India's exports to Canada rose 14.10% to $410 million.

Region-wise, North America (NAFTA) remained the largest market, accounting for 32.74% of India's pharmaceutical exports, although shipments to the region declined 1.75% to $6.2 billion.

Europe, which accounted for 20.47% of exports, recorded an 11.56% increase to $3.9 billion. Exports to Africa rose 6.45% to $2.7 billion, while Latin America and the Caribbean registered 17.92% growth to $1.5 billion.

Among other regions, Asean recorded the fastest growth of 22.89%, with exports reaching $1.2 billion.

On the import front, bulk drugs and drug intermediates remained India's largest import category, accounting for 44.84% of total pharmaceutical imports. Imports in the segment declined 2.46% to $2.5 billion.

Imports of formulations and biologicals increased 7.49% to $1.8 billion, while surgical imports rose 11.71% to $957.3 million. Vaccine imports increased 8.48% to $289.6 million. Imports of Ayush and herbal products declined 12.21% to $108.1 million.

China continued to be India's largest source of pharmaceutical imports, accounting for 36.30% of the total. Imports from China declined 2.27% to $2 billion during April-October FY27.

The US was the second-largest source, with imports increasing 7.56% to $543.3 million. Switzerland and the Netherlands followed, with imports of $393.8 million and $381.9 million, respectively. Imports from Italy rose 63.98% to $270.8 million.

Region-wise, Northeast Asia and Europe together accounted for nearly 80% of India's pharmaceutical imports.
